links.outcome: Medication alert rate and proportion of patients receiving alerts before vs after CDSS implementation
links.effect: Alert rate fell from 2.52% to 2.30% of orders; patients receiving alerts fell from 30.34% to 28.08%. Across 115 wards, 45.22% had fewer patients alerted and 20.87% had more.
links.quote: Among these, 130,286 (2.52%) and 133,562 (2.30%) prescriptions triggered alerts, indicating a significant reduction in the alert rate of 0.22%

unlisted_practices: Integrating a CDSS into pharmacist prescription review workflow

screen.reason: The study evaluates a standard rule-based/knowledge-based Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for medication prescription alerts rather than an artificial intelligence/machine learning model.
